newsitem.title: USA: Dow ends higher, but posts fourth biggest weekly loss.
newsitem.headline: Dow ends higher, but posts fourth biggest weekly loss.

text.p: The Dow Jones industrial average closed higher Friday after a tumultuous week that produced the fourth biggest weekly loss ever as speculation was rife that the Federal Reserve would raise interest rates again to slow the economy's growth.
The blue-chip Dow ended 48.72 points higher at 6,526.07, but for the week, it dropped 214.52 points -- the fourth largest after Oct. 13, 1989's fall of 216.26.
The record loss was still the 295.98-point fall in the week ended Oct. 23, 1987, the week of the Black Monday crash when the Dow had a one-day drop of 508 points.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,410 to 1,046 on active volume of 537 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
While investors expressed relief that the blood-letting on Wall Street abated, many said stocks were not ready to race back yet.
"I'd rather sell on strength than buy on dips here," said James Volk, director of equity trading at Jensen Securities.

Early in the session, the Dow crumbled more than 70 points following the release of the March employment report, which analysts said did nothing to dispel the belief that the Federal Reserve will hike interest rates again.

In March, average hourly wages rose by 5 cents to $12.15, after edging up a revised 5 cents in February, instead of the previously reported 3 cents, the Labour Department said. Over the past 12 months, wages rose 4 percent, matching their highest growth rate since the 12 months ended June 1990.
Concerns that a tight labour market might bring further Federal Reserve interest rate hikes sparked a sell-off in the bond market.
The 30-year Treasury bond fell 20/32, or $6.25 on a $1,000 bond, sending its yield up to 7.12 percent from 7.07 percent Thursday. Bond yields and prices move in opposite directions.
But stock investors appeared ready for some bargain hunting, particularily in high technology stocks.
Leading the way were semiconductor stocks, with Intel Corp., up 4-3/8 to 145 and Applied Materials Inc. up 3-3/4 to 52-1/4.
Among other rebounding high-tech shares was Dow industrial component Hewlett-Packard Co., which rose 2-1/8 to 52-3/4.
Market watchers said stocks could be finding a near-term low, with the Dow bouncing off the 6,400 level.
"If the bonds will behave I think the market could go back up for a while," said Bruce Bittles, market strategist at J.C. Bradford.
But the rebound on Friday may not mean the deep stock sell-off has run its course.
"You can have substantial rallies and still not be out of the woods yet," said Jonathan Dodd, technical analyst at Dean Witter.

Staples Inc. rose 5/8 to 21-7/8 and Office Depot Inc. sank 5-5/8 to 13-3/8 after the Federal Trade Commission voted to reject their proposed merger. Office Depot Chairman David Puente called the decision "absurd."
International Business Machines Corp. gave up 1-7/8 to 129-1/4. Merrill Lynch cut its near-term rating on the stock.

Checkpoint Systems Inc. lost 2-5/8 to 10-1/8 and Ultrak Inc. fell 4-5/8 to 11-7/8 after the two makers of security systems cancelled a $397 million merger agreement and projected lower-than-expected first quarter earnings.

Transport stocks rallied and oil shares slipped as oil prices sank in a market weakened by concerns about oversupply. On the New York Mercantile Exchange, May crude oil closed 35 cents lower at $19.12 a barrel.

Airlines stocks were among the companies that would benefit from lower fuel price. American Airlines' parent AMR Corp. shot up 3-7/8 to 86-3/8, and United Airlines' parent UAL Corp. jumped 4-7/8 at 69.
But oil companies fell. USX-Marathon Group eased 1/4 to 26-3/4 and Phillips Petroleum Co. lost 3/4 to 39-1/8.
The Nasdaq Composite index rose 22.97 points to 1,236.73.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks rose 7.58 to 757.90. The American Stock Exchange index was off 1.09 at 556.73.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks rose 3.62 to 398.02. The average share was up 37 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 7,213.962 up 76.35 or 1.07 percent.
